claims.sentence: On 29 May 2026, ahead of World No Tobacco Day, the WHO urged governments to protect young people from tobacco and nicotine addiction.
claims.evidence: WHO 29 May 2026 release 'urges governments to protect young people from addiction to tobacco and nicotine products' ahead of World No Tobacco Day.

claims.sentence: The WHO issued the call on 29 May 2026, ahead of World No Tobacco Day on 31 May.
claims.evidence: Release dated 29-05-2026; World No Tobacco Day is 31 May ('the day itself (31 May)').

claims.sentence: The WHO says at least 40 million children aged 13 to 15 use tobacco products, and that use of e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches among young people continues to rise.
claims.evidence: 'at least 40 million children aged 13-15 use tobacco products, and young people's use of e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches continues to rise'.

claims.sentence: It urges governments to ban flavoured products, ban advertising, promotion and sponsorship, make indoor public places completely smoke- and vape-free, and step up enforcement.
claims.evidence: Statement 'recommends banning flavoured products, banning advertising, promotion and sponsorship, making indoor public places completely smoke- and vape-free and stepping up enforcement'.

claims.sentence: On 29 May 2026, ahead of World No Tobacco Day on 31 May, the World Health Organization (WHO) urged governments to protect young people from addiction to tobacco and nicotine products.
The WHO says at least 40 million children aged 13 to 15 use tobacco products, and that young people's use of e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches continues to rise.
It says tobacco and nicotine companies are deliberately engineering products to be more appealing, easier to use and harder to quit, especially for adolescents.
claims.evidence: 'tobacco and nicotine companies are deliberately engineering their products to make them more appealing, easier to use and harder to quit, particularly for adolescents and young people'.

claims.sentence: The WHO calls on governments to ban flavoured products, ban advertising, promotion and sponsorship, make indoor public places completely smoke- and vape-free, and step up enforcement.
This is a global statement from the WHO and does not describe the rules in any one country.
claims.evidence: Editorial scope disclaimer; not a factual claim about WHO text.

notes: Search summaries only. Policy-ask list (flavours, advertising, smoke/vape-free, enforcement) and 'deliberately engineering' wording came from one summary attributed to the 29 May 2026 statement; PAHO hosts a copy (https://www.paho.org/en/news/29-5-2026-who-urges-governments-protect-young-people-addiction-tobacco-and-nicotine-products). c09 is an editorial disclaimer, not a WHO claim.
